title: Inscribed tags and jars of Tomb U-j, Abydos
note: Earliest known Egyptian writing: nearly 200 bone/ivory tags and 125 ink inscriptions, c. 3320 BCE (calibrated 14C, Boehmer, Dreyer and Kromer 1993; questioned by Hendrickx 2006). Sources: Visible Language chs. 5-6 (MacArthur, Stauder); Dreyer 1998 (DAI); Dee et al. 2013 (PMC3780825). Umm el-Qaab GeoNames 13535544 / OSM way 90456103.

title: Shang oracle-bone inscriptions at Anyang
note: Divination records of the last nine Shang kings, c. 1220-1050 BCE (Shaughnessy, Visible Language ch. 14); UNESCO WHC 1114 Yin Xu; Wu Ding and Consort Fu Hao divinations (a woman with a known tomb, 1975/76 discovery) could be a separate person record.

title: Early Zapotec glyphic inscriptions at San José Mogote and Monte Albán
note: Monument with two glyphs at San José Mogote dated by 14C to c. 600 BCE; Monte Albán writing c. 500-200 BCE (Palka, Visible Language ch. 15). Dating is debated; needs primary site reports (Marcus and Flannery) and coordinates for the archaeological site itself, not the village.

title: Early Maya writing at San Bartolo
note: Sub-V block text 300-200 BCE by AMS 14C (Saturno, Stuart and Beltrán, Science 2006); Las Pinturas murals c. 100 BCE. science.org returns 403; try the San Bartolo project copy or Peabody/Harvard sources.

title: Indus (Harappan) script
note: Undeciphered sign system of the mid-third millennium BCE; status as writing and possible cuneiform influence uncertain (Woods 2010). Perspectives needed on the linguistic versus non-linguistic debate; seals from Harappa and Mohenjo-daro (UNESCO WHC 138).

title: Proto-Elamite script
note: Undeciphered script of Susa and the Iranian plateau, c. 3100 BCE, possibly inspired by proto-cuneiform (Woods 2010). Under-recorded region for this period.

title: Clay tokens and sealed envelopes (bullae) of the Late Uruk period
note: Some 130 excavated envelopes, about 80 intact; Chogha Mish envelopes CT-scanned at the Oriental Institute; Schmandt-Besserat token theory versus Amiet/Zimansky/Woods critiques. Sources: sites.utexas.edu/dsb, Visible Language ch. 2.
